questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Primary adrenal insufficiency is eponymously:
questions.exp: 1° adrenal insufficiency = Addison's disease; 2° (m/c) follows abrupt steroid withdrawal, pituitary or hypothalamic dysfunction. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: The most common cause of SECONDARY adrenal insufficiency is:
questions.exp: 2° adrenal insufficiency (m/c overall pattern): abrupt steroid withdrawal is m/c, then pituitary and hypothalamic dysfunction. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: The most common cause of Addison's overall is:
questions.exp: Autoimmune is m/c overall: polyglandular autoimmune syndrome (PGA)/(APS) type 1 & 2 with anti 21-OH hydroxylase antibody (+), or isolated autoimmune adrenalitis. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Match the inherited cause — 1) Aladin gene mutation  2) X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy  3) T-pit mutation … A) ↑ very long chain fatty acid  B) Affects only corticotrophs  C) 3A/4A syndrome (alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, ANS)
questions.exp: Aladin mutation → 3A/4A syndrome (alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, 4th A = ANS); X-ALD → ↑ VLCFA; T-pit affects only corticotrophs. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: The m/c infective cause of Addison's in India is:
questions.exp: TB is m/c in India; meningococcaemia (children) causes Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Meningococcaemia in children causing adrenal haemorrhage is called:
questions.exp: Meningococcaemia (in children) → Waterhouse-Friderichsen syndrome. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: The adrenal gland size in Addison's may be:
questions.exp: Size in Addison's: enlarged, normal, atrophic, or asymmetrical. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Which group of features belongs to glucocorticoid (GC) deficiency?
opts: Asthenia, anorexia, weight loss, hypoglycaemia, eosinophilia
questions.exp: GC ↓↓↓: asthenia, anorexia, weakness, weight loss, fatigue, joint pain, hypoglycaemia + hypotension, postural hypotension, euvolemic hyponatremia, eosinophilia. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt craving and ↑BUN/creatinine (pre-renal) reflect deficiency of:
questions.exp: MC ↓↓↓: hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt cravings, ↑BUN & creatinine (d/t pre-renal failure). (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Dry atrophic skin, loss of axillary/pubic hair and loss of libido reflect loss of:
questions.exp: SS ↓↓↓: dry atrophic skin, loss of axillary & pubic hair, loss of libido. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: Hyperpigmentation in Addison's (from ↑ACTH) is seen in about:
questions.exp: ACTH ↑↑ → hyperpigmentation (90%) in sun-exposed areas and oral mucosa. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addison's disease: classification, causes and clinical features · p849
questions.q: The additional features listed are normocytic normochromic anemia and hypercalcaemia with:
opts: Auricular calcification (calcification absent in the adrenal gland)
questions.exp: Additional: normocytic normochromic anemia; hypercalcaemia → auricular calcification, while calcification is absent in the adrenal gland. (Book p849)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: The listed causes of weakness, fatigue and weight loss include TB, HIV, malignancy, lymphoma and:
questions.exp: Note: causes of weakness, fatigue & weight loss — TB, HIV, malignancy, lymphoma, Addison's disease. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: Addisonian crisis is precipitated by:
opts: Infection (any stress) and abrupt steroid withdrawal
questions.exp: Precipitated by infection (any stress) and abrupt steroid withdrawal. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: Features of Addisonian crisis include acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia and:
questions.exp: Crisis features: acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia, hypotension/circulatory failure; Rx fluids + steroids. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: Match 1° vs 2° adrenal insufficiency — 1) MC axis  2) ACTH  3) Hyperpigmentation … A) ↑ in 1°, ↓ in 2°  B) ↓ in 1°, normal (ACTH-independent) in 2°  C) + in 1°, − in 2°
questions.exp: MC is ↓ in 1° but normal (ACTH independent) in 2°; ACTH ↑ in 1°, ↓ in 2°; hyperpigmentation + in 1°, − in 2°. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: ‘Serum sodium falls in BOTH primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency.’
opts: False — sodium is normal in both
questions.exp: S. sodium ↓↓ in both; S. potassium ↑ only in 1° (normal in 2°). (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: Which pair of findings is present in 1° but ABSENT in 2° insufficiency?
opts: Loss of axillary hair and ↓ sodium
questions.exp: Salt craving/postural hypotension (+/−) and hyperpigmentation (+/−) distinguish 1° from 2°; axillary hair loss is ++ vs +. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: Vitiligo (autoimmune) is seen in:
questions.exp: Vitiligo (autoimmune) + in 1°, − in 2°. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: A fasting cortisol below what value diagnoses Addison's disease directly?
questions.exp: Fasting cortisol <3 µg/dL = Addison's; >20 µg/dL rules it out; 3–20 needs the Synacthen test. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: A fasting cortisol above what value rules out Addison's?
questions.exp: >20 µg/dL rules out Addison's. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: The Synacthen/ACTH stimulation test injects:
opts: 250 µg IM or IV synacthen/cosyntropin/synthetic ACTH
questions.exp: Inject 250 µg IM/IV synacthen (cosyntropin/synthetic ACTH); measure cortisol at 30 and 60 min (consider highest value). (Book p850)

questions.sec: Addisonian crisis, 1° vs 2° table and diagnostic tests · p850
questions.q: On the ACTH stimulation test, a peak cortisol below what value confirms Addison's?
questions.exp: <18 µg/dL confirms Addison's; >18 µg/dL rules it out. (Book p850)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: The drug of choice for maintenance in Addison's is:
questions.exp: Oral hydrocortisone is DOC; others prednisolone, dexamethasone; fludrocortisone if MC deficiency present. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: The maintenance hydrocortisone schedule (10 mg + 5 mg + 5 mg) totals:

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: Fludrocortisone (when MC deficiency is present) is dosed at:
questions.exp: Fludrocortisone dose: 50–100 µg. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: During fever or infection, the maintenance steroid dose should be:
questions.exp: Fever or infection: double the dose. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: On the day of surgery, the book advises:
questions.exp: On day of surgery: 50 to 100 mg IV hydrocortisone; hospitalisation ↑ dose to 50–75 mg/day. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: Match equivalent glucocorticoid doses — 1) Dexamethasone  2) Methylprednisolone  3) Prednisolone  4) Hydrocortisone … A) 20 mg  B) 0.75 mg  C) 4 mg  D) 5 mg
questions.exp: 0.75 mg dexamethasone = 4 mg methylprednisolone = 5 mg prednisolone = 20 mg hydrocortisone = 25 mg cortisol. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: In crisis, the FIRST-day hydrocortisone total (100 mg IV stat + 50 mg IV Q6H) equals:
questions.exp: 100 mg immediately + 50 mg IV Q6H = 1st day 300 mg; then 200 mg (2nd), 100 mg (3rd), 50 mg (4th). (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: Match the crisis taper by day — 1) 2nd day  2) 3rd day  3) 4th day … A) 100 mg IV  B) 200 mg IV  C) 50 mg IV
questions.exp: Day 2 = 200 mg IV, day 3 = 100 mg IV, day 4 = 50 mg IV, then oral 25 mg (10,10,5) for a week and 20 mg (10,5,5) maintenance ± fludrocortisone. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: Crisis IV fluids are given as:
opts: 0.9% NS/DNS 1 L over 1 hour, then 2–3 L over the next 12 hours
questions.exp: IV fluids: 0.9% NS/DNS 1 L over 1 hour, then 2–3 L over next 12 hours. (Book p851)

questions.sec: Treatment: maintenance, steroid equivalence and crisis regimen · p851
questions.q: After a crisis is controlled, the oral step-down before maintenance is:
questions.exp: Oral hydrocortisone 25 mg (10,10,5) for 1 week, then 20 mg (10,5,5) maintenance ± fludrocortisone. (Book p851)

units.title: Addison's disease: causes and hormone-deficiency features
units.guide: 1° = Addison's; 2° (m/c) = abrupt steroid withdrawal, pituitary/hypothalamic dysfunction. Causes: autoimmune m/c (PGA/APS 1&2, anti-21-OH antibody; isolated adrenalitis); inherited — Aladin (3A/4A: alacrimia, achalasia cardia, Addison's, ANS), X-ALD (↑VLCFA), T-pit (corticotrophs only); infective — TB m/c in India, meningococcaemia → Waterhouse-Friderichsen. Glands enlarged/normal/atrophic/asymmetrical. GC↓: asthenia, anorexia, weight loss, hypoglycaemia, euvolemic hyponatremia, eosinophilia; MC↓: hyperkalaemia, acidosis, hypovolemic hyponatremia, salt craving, ↑BUN/Cr; SS↓: dry skin, lost axillary/pubic hair, lost libido; ACTH↑: hyperpigmentation 90% (sun-exposed, oral mucosa); plus normocytic anemia and hypercalcaemia → auricular calcification (adrenal calcification absent).

units.title: Crisis, 1° vs 2° differences and the cortisol/Synacthen work-up
units.guide: Crisis precipitants: infection/any stress, abrupt steroid withdrawal; features acute abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation, hypoglycaemia, hypotension/circulatory failure; Rx fluids + steroids. 1° vs 2°: MC ↓ vs normal; ACTH ↑ vs ↓; pigmentation, salt craving/postural hypotension, vitiligo + vs −; K+ ↑ vs normal; Na+ ↓↓ both. Fasting cortisol <3 = Addison's, >20 rules out, 3–20 → Synacthen 250 µg IM/IV, peak <18 confirms, >18 rules out.

units.title: Replacement therapy: maintenance, equivalence and crisis protocol
units.guide: Maintenance oral hydrocortisone DOC 20 mg/day (10+5+5); prednisolone/dexamethasone alternatives; fludrocortisone 50–100 µg if MC deficiency. Fever/infection double dose; hospitalisation 50–75 mg/day; surgery day 50–100 mg IV. Equivalence 0.75 dexa = 4 methylpred = 5 prednisolone = 20 hydrocortisone = 25 cortisol. Crisis: 100 mg IV stat + 50 mg Q6H (day 1 = 300 mg), 200/100/50 mg days 2–4, oral 25 mg (10,10,5) ×1 week → 20 mg (10,5,5) ± fludrocortisone; fluids NS/DNS 1 L over 1 h then 2–3 L over 12 h.
